$comment: Contoso Health (fictional) access catalog: every access package, group and directory role the IGA rule files (birthright-rules.json, sod-rules.json) may name.
status 'terraform' = defined in lab/terraform and created when the named flag is on (NOT a claim that it exists in any tenant: no tenant has been built).
status 'planned'   = designed here, not defined anywhere yet. Scripts skip planned objects and say so; they never count them as clean.

tier follows ADR 0012: T1 privileged, T2 requestable, T3 birthright clinical. assignment: automatic (HR attributes, T3 only, no expiry) or request (approval + expiry, T1/T2). One model per package: a requestable extra on top of a birthright bundle is its own package (ICU - Float Access), never a second policy on the birthright one.

tests/Set-AutoAssignmentPolicies.Tests.ps1 checks every 'terraform' entry against the Terraform source, and modules/entitlement/tests/governance.tftest.hcl checks tier, assignment and resources of every Terraform package against this file, so neither side can drift.

accessPackages.name: Nurse - Clinical Apps
accessPackages.note: Birthright for nursing staff (ADR 0012 T3). Modelled assumption: the EHR role inside it carries break-the-glass (SOD-07).

accessPackages.name: ICU - Critical Care Apps
accessPackages.note: Birthright for ICU staff (ADR 0012 T3): automatic policy only, no request path, no expiry. Float and agency staff request 'ICU - Float Access' instead, so no SoD link ever has to sit on this package.

accessPackages.name: ICU - Float Access
accessPackages.note: Float and agency nurses covering ICU shifts (ADR 0012 T2): manager approval, 180-day expiry, re-request to keep it. Split from the ICU birthright package so SOD-01's preventive links can sit on the requestable side. Same apps as ICU - Critical Care Apps. verify: removing this assignment keeps a group membership the ICU birthright package also grants.

accessPackages.name: Prescriber - CPOE Ordering Apps
accessPackages.note: Prescribing follows medical-staff credentialing, not an HR job code, so it is requested (Medical Staff Office approves), never birthright.

groups.name: IGA-Access-Reviewers
groups.note: Today the fallback reviewer group is passed to modules/entitlement by object id only (access_review_fallback_group_object_id); this names it so SOD-08 can be evaluated.

groups.name: PIM-EHR-AuditLog-Admins
groups.note: In-app admin roles go through PIM for Groups (app-onboarding-intake.md field 7), so EHR audit-trail administration is a PIM group, not a package.

directoryRoles.name: Groups Administrator
directoryRoles.note: Template id checked on Microsoft Learn 'Microsoft Entra built-in roles' 2026-10-20. Treated as privileged here because it can change membership of any non-role-assignable group, incl. the App-* groups behind the packages (SOD-08). verify: whether Learn shows the PRIVILEGED label on it.

reviewTiers.$comment: How 10-Review-KPIs.ps1 assigns a review definition to a tier. First match wins: definition displayName prefix, then the access package + policy in the scope query (automatic policy = T3, request policy = the package's tier; a request policy left on a birthright package = T3), then any group / role in the scope query.

displayNamePrefixes.note: Stale-account review: outside the T1-T3 table in ADR 0012, reported on its own.

T3.source: ADR 0012: no human campaign; any T3 review is itself a finding
